text:
Garry Kasparov was born Garik Kimovich Weinstein in Baku, Azerbaijan SSR, and later adopted the surname Kasparov. He began serious chess study at age seven and trained under Vladimir Makogonov at Mikhail Botvinnik's chess school. Kasparov quickly rose through the ranks, winning the Soviet Junior Championship in 1976 and 1977. He became a Grandmaster in 1980, reaching the second rank behind Karpov in 1982.
His career milestones include becoming the youngest-ever world No. 1 player in January 1984. He secured the World Chess Championship in 1985 against Anatoly Karpov, and successfully defended his title in 1986 and 1987. Kasparov's rivalry with Karpov was significant, and after losing the title to Kramnik in 2000, he announced his retirement from regular competitive chess in March 2005. Post-retirement, he engaged in political activism, notably opposing Putin's government, and later worked with computer chess programs.
